title: Five-step walkthrough — Histogram as the worked example
description: Step by step, the exact wiring that turns a new folder under src/widgets/ into a fully usable widget — with the real Histogram snippets at every step.

data.markdown:
## What you will see

Each of the five sections below corresponds to one mandatory wiring point. The code in each section is **the real, current Histogram widget source** — copy these snippets, change `Histogram` → `<YourName>` and `histogram` → `<your-name>`, and you are 90% of the way to a new widget.

The contract is documented in `src/widgets/README.md`; this lesson dogfoods it by producing a Histogram render at the end (section 7) using only the artefacts the five steps create.

:::callout{type="info" title="Naming convention"}
- Folder name: `PascalCase` (`Histogram`, `ParametricExplorer`).
- `WidgetType` literal and section `type` field: `camelCase` (`histogram`, `parametricExplorer`).
- CSS variable name: `--widget-<kebab-case>` (`--widget-histogram`, `--widget-parametric-explorer`).
- JSON Schema filename emitted by `build:schemas`: `<kebab-case>.json` (`histogram.json`, `parametric-explorer.json`).
:::

## Step 1 of 5 — `src/styles/tokens.css`

The shared widget chrome (`src/widgets/Widget.tsx`) paints a 1-px accent rail on the left, an icon background tint, and the in-progress badge from a single CSS variable named `--widget-<name>`. Add it to **both** the light and dark theme blocks of `src/styles/tokens.css`:

```css
:root,
:root[data-theme="light"] {
  /* ... existing widget accents ... */
  --widget-histogram: #4e7a85;   /* muted teal */
}

:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  /* ... existing widget accents ... */
  --widget-histogram: #82b3bd;   /* lighter for dark backgrounds */
}
```

Existing accents (light theme) — pick a tasteful, low-saturation colour distinct from these:

| widget    | accent     |
| --------- | ---------- |
| theory    | `#56524a`  |
| demo      | `#2563eb`  |
| quiz      | `#6b3eaa`  |
| code      | `#0d7a5f`  |
| sandbox   | `#b45309`  |
| histogram | `#4e7a85`  |

The accent is intentionally muted: lessons should foreground content, not chrome.

:::callout{type="warning" title="Forgetting one theme block"}
If you only add the CSS var to `[data-theme="light"]`, the widget will render correctly in light mode and lose its accent rail in dark mode (or vice versa). Both blocks always.
:::

Step 4 — Add the per-widget editor form
Result — Histogram rendered from a section that exercises all 5 steps

data.markdown:
The histogram you see above is rendered from this exact section in the lesson JSON:

```json
{
  "id": "s6-histogram-final-render",
  "title": "Result — ...",
  "type": "histogram",
  "data": {
    "binEdges": [-4.5, -3.5, -2.5, -1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5],
    "counts": [3, 13, 60, 175, 240, 175, 60, 13, 3]
  }
}
```

For that JSON to load and render, every one of the five steps had to be in place:

1. The accent rail and slider thumb on the chart pull `--widget-histogram` from `tokens.css`.
2. The `data` object was validated by `HistogramDataSchema` (Zod) on lesson load.
3. The renderer found `histogram` in `widgetRegistry` and dispatched to `HistogramWidget`.
4. (Not exercised by read-only lesson view — only relevant when editing.)
5. The `SectionSchema` discriminated union accepted `type: 'histogram'` with `data: HistogramData`, otherwise the lesson file would have been rejected before the page rendered.

sections.title: Quick check: what does Step 5 protect against?

data.question: You add a new widget and complete steps 1–4 (CSS var, Zod schema + build.ts entry, registry entry, editor) but skip step 5 (SectionSchema variant). What is the most likely failure mode?
options: The widget never appears on the page — `SectionRenderer` cannot find a component for the new section type.
The widget renders during a hot-reload session, but lesson JSON containing it is rejected by `PUT /api/courses/.../lessons/...` and on the next cold-start when the validator re-checks files on disk.
TypeScript fails to compile because `widgetRegistry` is incomplete.
`npm run build:schemas` errors because the schema is missing from `src/widgets/schemas/build.ts`.
data.explanation: Step 5 is the API/validation layer. Without it, the widget renders in-memory because `widgetRegistry` is sufficient for the read path, but every persistence boundary that runs `LessonSchema.parse(...)` rejects the section. The other options describe failures of *different* steps: option A is what happens when you skip step 3 (registry); option C is what happens when you forget the `WidgetType` literal in step 3; option D is what happens when you skip the `build.ts` part of step 2.
